Predictions from a choice model

Source: R/methods.R
predict.choicemodel.Rd

Predictions from a choice model

Usage

# S3 method for class 'choicemodel'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("prob", "class", "link", "prob_outcome", "regime", "prob_conditional",
    "posterior", "ranking"),
  offset = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A "choicemodel" fit.

newdata

Optional data frame (same layout as the fit: for the long layout it must contain the id and alt columns, one row per available alternative; the choice indicator is not needed). It must hold every covariate of every equation (for an inflated fit the split-equation variables too) and, for a fixed-effects fit, the unit column (only units seen in the fit). Factor levels must be among those of the fit. With NULL, the estimation cases.

type

"prob" (default): the \(n \times J\) matrix of probabilities of the observed alternatives, \(P^*\) (for a random-intercept fit the population-averaged probabilities); "class": the modal alternative (a factor); "link": the \(n \times J\) matrix of utilities \(V_{ij}\) (\(-\infty\) where unavailable); for nested-logit fits "prob_conditional": the probabilities of the alternatives within their nests, \(P(j \mid \text{nest})\); for inflated models also "prob_outcome": the outcome-stage probabilities \(P_{ij}\) (the choice probabilities of a case in the choice regime, which is what Bagozzi and Marchetti (2017) hold the split equation at when comparing BIMNL and MNL effects), "regime": \(P(s_i = 1 \mid z_i)\), the probability of not being an inflated (always-\(k\)) case (with several inflated alternatives the matrix of the regime probabilities: the choice regime, then captivity to each inflated alternative), and "posterior" (estimation cases only): the probability of the choice regime given the observed choice, \(\phi_i P_{ik} / P^*_{ik}\) for a case that chose \(k\) and 1 otherwise, which separates routine from occasional choosers of \(k\) (with several inflated alternatives the matrix of the regime posteriors); for rank-ordered logit fits also "ranking" (estimation cases only): the probability of each observed ranking. For a rank-ordered fit "prob" and "class" describe first choices.

offset

Offset for newdata when the fit has one (an \(n \times J\) matrix in the wide layout, a vector aligned to the rows in the long layout; a long-layout fit whose offset was a column name finds it in newdata). A fit with an offset refuses newdata without one.

...

Unused.

Value

A matrix (rows named by case), a factor, or a numeric vector.
